questions.question: Sa pangungusap na “Malamig ang simoy ng hangin,” ano ang pinakamalapit na kahulugan ng “simoy”?
questions.note: Ang simoy ay banayad na galaw o daloy ng hangin.

questions.question: Alin ang wastong gamit ng “nang” sa pangungusap?
questions.note: Ginagamit ang nang sa pang-abay na paraan o panahon, gaya ng “nang maaga.”

questions.question: Ano ang ipinahihiwatig ng sawikaing “makapal ang mukha”?

choices.B: Walang hiya o hindi madaling mapahiya

questions.note: Tumutukoy ito sa kawalan ng hiya o pagiging hindi alintana ang puna.

questions.question: Which part of the body is the 'siko'?
questions.note: Tuhod = knee, balikat = shoulder, pulso = wrist.

questions.question: What does 'masarap' mean?
questions.note: Maanghang = spicy, mahal = expensive, sobrang luto = overcooked.

questions.question: Who is called 'Kuya' in a Filipino family?
questions.note: Kuya is the respectful term for an older brother or older male.

questions.question: What is 'apatnapu' in English?
questions.note: Labing-apat = 14, apat na raan = 400, animnapu = 60.

questions.question: Which Tagalog word means 'cloud'?
questions.note: Ulan = rain, hangin = wind, kidlat = lightning.

questions.question: Which word is the opposite of 'mabigat'?
questions.note: Mabigat = heavy; magaan = light. Makapal = thick, malambot = soft, matibay = sturdy.

questions.question: Who is your 'pamangkin'?
questions.note: Pinsan = cousin, apo = grandchild, inaanak = godchild.

questions.question: Alin ang pinakamalinaw na pagkakaiba ng “Nagsulat si Lira ng liham” at “Sinulatan ni Lira ang guro”?

choices.A: Ang una ay actor-focus; ang ikalawa ay may patient/locative focus sa pandiwang sinulatan.
choices.B: Ang una ay nasa aspektong nagaganap; ang ikalawa ay pawatas
choices.C: Ang ikalawa ay nangangahulugang ang guro ang sumulat
choices.D: Pareho silang pangungusap na walang pandiwa

questions.note: Nagbabago ang pokus at papel na binibigyang-diin ng pandiwa.

questions.question: Sa “Hindi siya sumama, bagkus ay nagpaiwan,” ano ang ipinahihiwatig ng “bagkus”?

choices.A: Pagwawasto o pagpapalit sa inaasahang kilos

questions.note: Ang bagkus ay naglalahad ng kabaligtaran o pamalit na kilos.

questions.question: Aling pangungusap ang gumagamit nang wasto ng “kung” at “kong”?

choices.B: Hindi ko alam kung darating siya; ito ang aklat kong hiniram.
choices.C: Kung aklat kong hiniram, ibalik mo.
choices.D: Hindi ko alam kong darating siya; ito ang aklat kung hiniram.

questions.note: Kung introduces a condition or indirect question; kong is a contraction of ko + -ng.

questions.question: Ano ang kahulugan ng “makapal ang mukha” sa karaniwang idyomatikong gamit?

choices.B: Matapang dahil sa pisikal na lakas
choices.C: Walang hiya o hindi madaling mapahiya

questions.note: Idyoma ito para sa kawalan ng hiya, hindi literal na paglalarawan.

questions.question: Sa “Ipinagluto ni Ana ng lugaw ang maysakit,” sino ang benepisyaryo ng kilos?
questions.note: Ang ipinagluto ay nagmamarka ng kilos na ginawa para sa isang tao.

questions.question: Ano ang pangunahing tungkulin ng “pala” sa “Ikaw pala ang bagong guro”?

choices.C: Pagpapakita ng bagong natuklasan o napagtanto

questions.note: Ang pala ay discourse particle na nagpapahiwatig ng pagkakatuklas.

questions.question: Alin ang mas angkop na kahulugan ng “marahuyo” kaysa simpleng “magustuhan”?
questions.note: Mas matindi ang pagkabighani na ipinahihiwatig ng marahuyo.

questions.question: Sa “Kung hindi dahil sa babala, napahamak sana sila,” ano ang ugnayan ng mga sugnay?

choices.C: Di-naganap na kondisyon at di-naganap na bunga

questions.note: Ang sana ay nagpapahiwatig ng resultang maaaring nangyari sa ibang kondisyon.

questions.question: Ano ang ipinahihiwatig ng “umano” sa ulat?

choices.C: Ang pahayag ay iniuulat ngunit hindi ganap na pinatutunayan ng nagsasalita

questions.note: Nagmamarka ito ng iniulat o sinasabing impormasyon na may distansiya ang tagapag-ulat.

questions.question: Aling pares ang pinakamalapit sa pagkakaiba ng “masinop” at “maramot”?

choices.B: Maingat at mahusay gumamit ng yaman; ayaw gumastos kahit nararapat

questions.note: Ang pagiging masinop ay maingat na pamamahala, samantalang ang maramot ay labis na pag-iwas magbigay o gumastos.

questions.question: Sa “Ikinagalit ng konseho ang pasyang ipinataw nang walang konsultasyon,” ano ang binibigyang-diin ng “ikinagalit”?

choices.B: Ang pasya bilang sanhi ng galit
choices.C: Ang konseho bilang tagaganap ng paggalit sa iba
choices.D: Ang kilos na magaganap pa lamang

questions.note: Ang ikina- construction ay karaniwang nagmamarka ng sanhi o pinagmulan ng damdamin.

questions.question: Alin ang pinakamahusay na paliwanag sa pagkakaiba ng “Nabasa ko ang liham” at “Binasa ko ang liham”?

choices.A: Maaaring di-sinasadyang pagkatuklas/pagkakabasa ang nabasa; sinadyang pagbasa ang binasa.
choices.D: Pareho silang laging nangangahulugang nabasa sa ulan

questions.note: Nag-iiba ang aspektuwal at semantikong diin: nabasa can imply came to read/was able to read, binasa emphasizes the act.

questions.question: Sa “Hindi lamang siya mahusay magsalita kundi marunong ding makinig,” anong lohikal na relasyon ang ipinapakita?

choices.A: Pagdaragdag ng ikalawang katangiang nagpapalawak sa una

questions.note: Ang hindi lamang…kundi…din ay additive correlative construction.

questions.question: Bakit hindi eksaktong magkasingkahulugan ang “dangal” at “karangalan” sa lahat ng konteksto?

choices.A: Maaaring tumukoy ang dangal sa integridad o dignidad, samantalang ang karangalan ay maaari ring tumukoy sa pagkilalang iginawad.
choices.B: Walang kahulugan ang dangal sa Filipino
choices.D: Ang dangal ay pandiwa at karangalan ay pang-abay

questions.note: Magkalapit ang kahulugan ngunit nagkakaiba ang kolokasyon at diin.

questions.question: Ano ang epekto ng paglalagay ng “pa” sa “May natitira” upang maging “May natitira pa”?

choices.D: Ipinahihiwatig na nagpapatuloy o hindi pa nauubos ang natitira.

questions.note: Ang pa ay nagdaragdag ng kahulugang still/yet.

questions.question: Alin ang pinakamainam na pagbasa sa salawikaing “Nasa Diyos ang awa, nasa tao ang gawa”?

choices.A: Hindi dapat gumawa ng anumang hakbang
choices.B: Garantisado ang tagumpay kahit walang pagsisikap
choices.C: Ang gawa ng tao ay walang kabuluhan
choices.D: Hindi sapat ang pag-asa lamang; may pananagutan ding kumilos ang tao.

questions.note: Pinag-uugnay nito ang pananampalataya at sariling pagkilos.

questions.question: Sa “Ipinagkait sa mga magsasaka ang patas na kabayaran,” ano ang ipinahihiwatig ng pandiwa?

choices.B: May benepisyong dapat sana nilang matanggap ngunit hindi ibinigay.
choices.C: Walang usapin ng katarungan sa pangungusap
choices.D: Sila ang kusang tumanggi sa lahat ng kabayaran

questions.note: Ang pagkakait ay hindi pagbibigay ng inaasahan o nararapat na bagay.

questions.question: Alin ang pinakamahusay na halimbawa ng eupemismo?
questions.note: Ang eupemismo ay mas banayad na pananalita para sa sensitibong paksa.

questions.question: Sa pagsusuri ng tula, ano ang pagkakaiba ng persona at makata?

choices.A: Ang makata ay tauhan lamang sa bawat tula
choices.B: Ang persona ay pamagat ng tula
choices.C: Ang persona ang tinig na nagsasalita sa tula; hindi kailangang siya mismo ang makata.
choices.D: Laging iisa ang persona at makata

questions.note: Dapat ihiwalay ang tekstuwal na tinig sa tunay na may-akda.

questions.question: Ano ang pinakamalakas na palatandaan na metapora, hindi literal na pahayag, ang “siya ang ilaw ng tahanan”?

choices.A: May sukat na watts ang tao
choices.B: Iniuugnay ang tao sa ilaw upang ipahiwatig ang gabay o pag-asa.
choices.C: Nasa madilim na silid ang tao

questions.note: Ang metapora ay naglilipat ng kahulugan batay sa pagkakatulad.

questions.question: Sa “Ipinangamba ng mga residente ang biglang pagtaas ng tubig,” bakit angkop ang “ipinangamba”?

choices.A: Nangangahulugan itong natapos na ang baha
choices.B: Tumutukoy ito sa pagmamay-ari ng tubig
choices.C: Ipinakikita nitong ang mga residente ang kinatatakutan ng tubig
choices.D: Ipinakikita nito ang pangyayari bilang pinagmumulan ng pangamba.

questions.note: Ang ipinangamba ay sanhi/trigger ng damdaming pangamba.

questions.question: Alin ang pinakamalinaw na pagkakaiba ng “kung sakali” at “sakaling”?

choices.A: Ang kung sakali ay laging nakaraan; sakaling ay laging hinaharap
choices.B: Walang kondisyunal na kahulugan ang alinman
choices.C: Pareho silang maaaring magpakilala ng kondisyon; ang sakaling ay mas madalas direktang nag-uugnay sa sugnay.

questions.note: Pareho ang kondisyunal na gamit ngunit magkaiba ang sintaktikong distribusyon.

questions.question: Sa “Hindi raw siya ang may sala,” ano ang saklaw ng “raw”?

choices.D: Iniuulat na pagtanggi o pahayag ng ibang tao, hindi awtomatikong pag-endorso ng nagsasalita.

questions.note: Ang raw/daw ay evidential o reportative particle.

questions.question: Bakit mahalagang tingnan ang konteksto sa salitang “liban”?

choices.B: Maaari itong mangahulugang bukod/maliban sa isang bagay o tumukoy sa pagliban, depende sa anyo at gamit.
choices.D: Iisa lamang ang kahulugan nito sa lahat ng pangungusap

questions.note: Maaaring magbago ang interpretasyon batay sa sintaks at kolokasyon.

questions.question: Sa “Nagpasiya ang lupon matapos timbangin ang magkakasalungat na salaysay,” ano ang ipinahihiwatig ng “timbangin”?

choices.B: Suriin at paghambingin nang maingat ang ebidensiya, hindi literal na sukatin.

questions.note: Matalinghagang gamit ito para sa maingat na pagsusuri.

questions.question: Alin ang wastong pagsusuri sa “Pinag-usapan nila ang panukala” kumpara sa “Pinag-usapan nila ang isa’t isa”?

choices.B: Ang ikalawa ay nangangahulugang nag-away sila
choices.C: Sa una, paksa ang panukala; sa ikalawa, ang isa’t isa ang kapwa kalahok na paksa ng usapan.

questions.note: Ang pandiwa at layon ang nagtatakda ng interpretasyon.

questions.question: Ano ang ipinahihiwatig ng “di-maikakaila” sa isang argumento?

choices.B: Ipinapakita ng may-akda na itinuturing niyang mahirap itanggi ang pahayag, ngunit kailangan pa rin ng ebidensiya.
choices.C: Isa itong tanong na walang sagot
choices.D: Awtomatikong totoo ang pahayag kahit walang patunay

questions.note: Ang retorikal na paninindigan ay hindi kapalit ng ebidensiya.

questions.question: Sa “Nang makita niya ang tala, saka niya napagtanto ang pagkakamali,” ano ang tungkulin ng “saka”?

choices.B: Ipinapakita ang pagkakasunod at kaugnayan ng dalawang pangyayari.

questions.note: Ang saka ay nagmamarka ng kasunod na pangyayari o hakbang.

questions.question: Bakit hindi sapat na sabihing “pareho lang” ang “daw” at “raw” sa lahat ng pangungusap?

choices.A: Ang daw ay pangngalan at raw ay pang-uri
choices.B: Magkaiba sila ng panahon ng pandiwa
choices.C: May tuntuning ponolohikal sa pagpili ng anyo batay sa tunog na sinusundan.
choices.D: Ang raw ay ginagamit lamang sa tula

questions.note: Karaniwang ginagamit ang raw pagkatapos ng patinig at ilang tunog; ang daw sa ibang kapaligiran.

questions.question: Sa kritikal na pagbasa, ano ang dapat gawin kapag ang isang pahayag ay puno ng matitinding salitang tulad ng “walang duda” ngunit walang sanggunian?

choices.A: Ituring na mali agad nang walang pagsusuri
choices.B: Tanggapin ito dahil matatag ang pananalita
choices.C: Ihiwalay ang retorikal na katiyakan sa ebidensiyang tunay na sumusuporta sa pahayag.
choices.D: Suriin lamang ang haba ng pangungusap

questions.note: Ang tono ng katiyakan ay hindi nagpapatunay sa katotohanan.

questions.question: Sa “Ikinabahala ng mga iskolar ang pagbura sa mga salitang katutubo,” anong ugnayang semantiko ang ipinapakita ng ikina-?

choices.A: Ang pagbura ang sanhi ng pagkabahala ng mga iskolar.
choices.C: Ang mga iskolar ang sanhi ng pagbura
choices.D: Ang pagbura ay benepisyaryo ng kilos

questions.note: Ang ikina- construction ay nagpapakilala ng sanhi ng damdamin o kalagayan.

questions.question: Paano nagbabago ang pananaw sa “Sinunod ng bata ang utos” at “Sinunod sa bata ang utos” kung ituturing na magkaibang istruktura?

choices.A: Sa ikalawa, tiyak na ang bata ang nagbigay ng utos
choices.B: Sa una, ang utos ang tagasunod
choices.C: Sa una, malinaw na ang bata ang tagasunod; ang ikalawa ay hindi karaniwang katumbas at nangangailangan ng ibang konteksto o pagsusuri.
choices.D: Pareho silang natural at eksaktong magkapareho

questions.note: Ang pokus at argument structure ay hindi mapagpapalit nang walang pagbabago.

questions.question: Ano ang masusing pagbasa sa “Mabuti na lamang at nakinig siya”?

choices.A: Ipinahihiwatig ng na lamang at at ang ginhawa o positibong pagtingin sa naganap na pakikinig.
choices.C: Neutral na ulat ito na walang saloobin

questions.note: Ang parirala ay may evaluative/pragmatic meaning.

questions.question: Sa pangungusap na “Maaaring makatwiran ang pasya, subalit hindi makatarungan ang proseso,” anong pagkakaiba ang pinaninindigan?

choices.A: Magkapareho ang makatwiran at makatarungan sa lahat ng konteksto
choices.B: Maaaring maging katanggap-tanggap ang resulta ngunit may depekto ang paraang ginamit upang marating ito.
choices.C: Tiyak na ilegal ang bawat pasya
choices.D: Ang proseso ay hindi mahalaga kung mabuti ang resulta

questions.note: Ibinubukod ang lohikal na katwiran sa pagiging makatarungan ng pamamaraan.

questions.question: Bakit maaaring maging mapanlinlang ang pagsasalin ng “hiya” bilang simpleng “shame”?

choices.A: Saklaw ng hiya ang panlipunang dangal, paggalang, pag-iingat sa ugnayan, at pagkapahiya depende sa konteksto.
choices.B: Ang hiya ay laging nangangahulugang takot
choices.C: Walang katumbas na kahulugan ang hiya sa Filipino
choices.D: Ang shame ay mas malawak sa lahat ng konteksto

questions.note: Ang mga konseptong kultural ay hindi laging tumutugma nang isa-sa-isa sa pagsasalin.

questions.question: Sa “Kahit na kinilala ang kanyang ambag, ipinagkait pa rin sa kanya ang kapangyarihang magpasya,” ano ang kontrast?

choices.A: Ang pagkilala ay awtomatikong nagbibigay ng awtoridad
choices.B: May pagkilala sa ambag ngunit walang katumbas na awtoridad o kapangyarihan.
choices.C: Parehong tinanggihan ang ambag at kapangyarihan

questions.note: Pinaghihiwalay ng kahit na at pa rin ang pagkilala sa resulta.

questions.question: Ano ang pagkakaiba ng denotasyon at konotasyon sa pagsusuri ng salitang “ahas” na ginamit sa paglalarawan ng tao?

choices.B: Ang konotasyon ay baybay ng salita
choices.D: Ang denotasyon ay hayop; ang konotasyon sa tao ay pagtataksil o panlilinlang.

questions.note: Ang konotasyon ay dagdag na asosasyong kultural o emosyonal.

questions.question: Kung paulit-ulit na ginagamit ng isang sanaysay ang “diumano” sa paratang, ano ang posibleng epekto?

choices.B: Nilalagyan ng distansiya ang paratang at ipinahihiwatig na hindi ito itinatanghal bilang napatunayang katotohanan.
choices.C: Tinatanggal nito ang pangangailangan sa sanggunian

questions.note: Ang reportative marker ay naghihiwalay sa iniulat at napatunayan.

questions.question: Paano nakatutulong ang pag-aaral sa aspektong naganap, nagaganap, at magaganap sa interpretasyon ng salaysay?

choices.B: Tinutukoy lamang nito ang kasarian ng tauhan
choices.C: Pinapalitan nito ang lahat ng pang-abay
choices.D: Natutukoy kung ang kilos ay natapos, nagpapatuloy, o inaasahang mangyari, bagaman mahalaga pa rin ang konteksto.

questions.note: Ang aspektong pandiwa ay nag-aambag sa pag-unawa sa panahon at daloy ng salaysay.

questions.question: Sa pag-aanalisa ng bugtong o salawikain, bakit dapat iwasan ang sobrang literal na pagbasa?

choices.A: Maaaring gumamit ito ng metapora, paralelismo, at kulturang pahiwatig na hindi nahuhuli sa literal na kahulugan.
choices.C: Lahat ng salawikain ay walang lohika
choices.D: Hindi kailanman mahalaga ang mga salita

questions.note: Ang matalinghagang anyo ay nangangailangan ng kontekstuwal at kultural na pagbasa.

questions.question: Sa “Hindi sa hindi siya sumang-ayon, kundi sa paraang ipinataw ang kasunduan,” anong uri ng paglilinaw ang ginagawa?

choices.A: Itinatama ang posibleng maling pagbasa: hindi ang pagsang-ayon ang tinututulan kundi ang proseso.
choices.D: Tinatanggihan ang parehong kasunduan at proseso

questions.note: Ang hindi sa X kundi sa Y ay naglilipat ng pokus sa eksaktong punto ng pagtutol.

questions.question: Ano ang pangunahing pagkakaiba ng pokus sa tagaganap at pokus sa layon sa Filipino?

choices.A: Ang pokus sa layon ay walang pandiwa
choices.B: Laging nauuna ang tagaganap sa pokus sa layon
choices.C: Ipinapakita ng panlapi at estruktura kung aling kalahok ang ginagawang sentro ng pangungusap, hindi simpleng kung sino ang “gumagawa.”
choices.D: Walang kaugnayan ang panlapi sa pokus

questions.note: Ang voice/focus system ay nag-aayos ng ugnayan ng pandiwa at mga kalahok.

questions.question: Bakit hindi laging maaaring ipagpalit ang “dahil sa” at “dahil kay” sa Filipino?

choices.A: Ang dahil sa ay laging nagpapahayag ng layunin
choices.B: Ang dahil kay ay ginagamit lamang sa lugar
choices.D: Karaniwang sinusundan ng dahil sa ang pangyayari/bagay o pariralang pangngalan, samantalang kay ay ginagamit sa pantanging pangalan ng tao.

questions.note: Magkaiba ang pang-ukol na pinipili batay sa uri ng kasunod na parirala.

questions.question: Sa pagsusuri ng pahayag na “Ang katahimikan niya ay sagot na rin,” ano ang kailangang patunayan bago ituring na makatotohanang konklusyon?

choices.A: Na ang katahimikan ay laging pagsang-ayon
choices.B: Na sa konteksto, ang katahimikan ay may sapat na batayan upang ipakahulugang sagot, hindi lamang kawalan ng tugon.
choices.D: Na hindi kailangang alamin ang konteksto

questions.note: Ang interpretasyong pragmatiko ay umaasa sa konteksto at alternatibong paliwanag.

questions.question: Alin ang pinakamainam na paliwanag kung bakit hindi magkasingkahulugan ang “pagpapakumbaba” at “pagpapahiya”?

choices.A: Ang una ay maaaring kusang pagkilala sa limitasyon; ang ikalawa ay pagdulot ng kahihiyan, madalas mula sa iba.

questions.note: Magkaiba ang kusang asal at kilos na nagpapababa sa dangal ng iba.

questions.question: Sa pananalitang “Kung tutuusin, hindi ang kakulangan sa datos ang problema kundi ang paraan ng pagbasa rito,” ano ang retorikal na galaw?

choices.A: Inililipat ang sanhi ng problema mula sa dami ng datos tungo sa interpretasyon nito.

questions.note: Ang contrastive construction ay nagtutuwid ng diagnosis ng problema.

questions.question: Bakit dapat pag-ibahin ang salitang “bayan” sa kahulugang pamayanan at sa kahulugang bansa sa isang tekstong historikal?

choices.A: Dahil walang historikal na pagbabago ang wika
choices.B: Dahil iisa lamang ang kahulugan ng bayan
choices.C: Maaaring magbago ang politikal na saklaw ng salita ayon sa panahon at konteksto.
choices.D: Dahil ang bayan ay hindi kailanman tumutukoy sa tao

questions.note: Ang semantikong saklaw ng salita ay historikal at kontekstuwal.

questions.question: Sa “Sadyang hindi niya sinabi ang buong katotohanan,” ano ang naiiba sa “Hindi niya sinasadyang sabihin ang buong katotohanan”?

choices.A: Sa una, sinadya ang hindi pagsasabi; sa ikalawa, hindi sinadya ang mismong pagsasabi o ang kinalabasan nito.
choices.C: Sa ikalawa, malinaw na nagsinungaling siya

questions.note: Nagbabago ang saklaw ng negasyon at sinasadya dahil sa ayos ng salita.

questions.question: Ano ang pinakamabisang paraan upang suriin kung ang salawikain ay ginagamit nang angkop sa isang argumento?

choices.A: Suriin kung talagang sinusuportahan ng aral nito ang konklusyon at kung ang konteksto ay katulad ng ipinahihiwatig.
choices.B: Gamitin ito upang palitan ang lahat ng datos

questions.note: Ang kasabihan ay maaaring magbigay ng pananaw ngunit hindi awtomatikong patunay.

questions.question: Sa pagsusuri ng salin, bakit kailangang tingnan ang rehistro at kausap bukod sa literal na kahulugan?

choices.A: Dahil hindi mahalaga ang literal na kahulugan
choices.B: Dahil maaaring magbago ang antas ng paggalang, pagiging pormal, o tono kahit tama ang literal na salin.
choices.C: Dahil ang rehistro ay tumutukoy lamang sa baybay
choices.D: Dahil lahat ng salin ay dapat magkapareho ang haba

questions.note: Ang pragmatikong katumbas ay nangangailangan ng angkop na tono at relasyon ng mga nagsasalita.

questions.question: Why did early river-valley states often develop near large rivers?

choices.B: Floodplains supplied water and fertile soil, supporting food surpluses
choices.C: Rivers eliminated the need for government
choices.D: River water made metal tools unnecessary

questions.note: Reliable water and fertile alluvium supported intensive agriculture and larger settlements.

questions.question: Which feature most clearly distinguishes a primary source from a later historical account?

choices.B: It was created during the period or by a participant/witness being studied

questions.note: Primary sources originate in the period or from participants, though they still require critical evaluation.

questions.question: Why did the Roman Republic develop checks such as separate magistracies and a Senate?

choices.A: To guarantee equal power for every resident
choices.B: To limit concentration of authority among competing elites and offices

questions.note: Republican institutions distributed authority, though political equality remained limited.

questions.question: Which ship sank in 1912 after striking an iceberg?
questions.note: The Lusitania was torpedoed in 1915; the Britannic hit a mine in 1916.

questions.question: Who co-wrote 'The Communist Manifesto' with Friedrich Engels?
questions.note: Published in 1848, decades before Lenin's revolution.

questions.question: Whose 1492 voyage reached the Americas for Spain?
questions.note: Da Gama sailed to India for Portugal; Magellan's voyage began in 1519.

questions.question: In which country did the Renaissance begin?
questions.note: It began in Italian city-states like Florence in the 14th century.

questions.question: Who led Nazi Germany during World War II?
questions.note: Mussolini led Fascist Italy; Bismarck and Wilhelm II were earlier German leaders.

questions.question: Which city was divided by a wall from 1961 to 1989?
questions.note: The Berlin Wall fell on November 9, 1989.

questions.question: Which civilization built Machu Picchu?
questions.note: Built in the Peruvian Andes in the 15th century.

questions.question: Bakit mas kapaki-pakinabang ang paghahambing ng tax records at personal diaries kaysa umasa sa isa lamang?

choices.A: Dahil walang bias ang tax records
choices.B: Maaaring ipakita ng magkakaibang uri ng sanggunian ang parehong lipunan mula sa magkaibang pananaw.
choices.C: Dahil ang dalawang uri ay hindi maaaring magkasalungat

questions.note: Triangulation helps test claims and reveal perspective.

questions.question: Paano nakatulong ang pag-imprenta sa paglaganap ng Repormasyon?

choices.A: Pinalitan nito ang lahat ng simbahan
choices.B: Ginawa nitong walang silbi ang mga wika
choices.C: Agad nitong inalis ang lahat ng pagkakaiba sa relihiyon
choices.D: Pinababa nito ang gastos at pinabilis ang pagpaparami at pagkalat ng mga polyeto at salin.

questions.note: Printing amplified circulation; it did not mechanically guarantee uniform belief.

questions.question: Bakit nag-iba ang epekto ng Black Death sa iba’t ibang rehiyon ng Europa?

choices.A: Pare-pareho ang populasyon at ekonomiya sa lahat ng lugar
choices.B: Walang kaugnayan ang kalakalan sa pagkalat
choices.C: Nagkakaiba ang demograpiya, kalakalan, institusyon, at tugon ng mga pamahalaan at komunidad.
choices.D: Iisang patakaran ang ipinatupad sa buong Europa

questions.note: Local conditions shaped mortality and social consequences.

questions.question: Ano ang mahalagang pagkakaiba ng imperyalismo at kolonyalismo?

choices.A: Ang imperyalismo ay mas malawak na pagpapalawak ng kapangyarihan; ang kolonyalismo ay karaniwang direktang kontrol at paninirahan/pamamahala sa teritoryo.
choices.B: Magkapareho sila sa lahat ng gamit
choices.C: Ang imperyalismo ay tumutukoy lamang sa kalakalan
choices.D: Ang kolonyalismo ay laging walang pamamahala

questions.note: The terms overlap but describe different scales and mechanisms.

questions.question: Bakit hindi sapat na tawaging “demokratiko” ang isang sinaunang polis dahil lamang may pagtitipon ng mamamayan?

choices.A: Dahil walang polis na may pagtitipon
choices.B: Maaaring ibinukod nito ang kababaihan, alipin, at mga dayuhang residente sa pagkamamamayan.
choices.C: Dahil ang demokrasya ay nangangailangan ng hari
choices.D: Dahil lahat ng sinaunang lipunan ay may unibersal na karapatan

questions.note: Participation depended on restrictive definitions of citizenship.

questions.question: Paano pinahina ng inflation pagkatapos ng Unang Digmaang Pandaigdig ang ilang pamahalaan?

choices.A: Maaari nitong sirain ang ipon, pahinain ang tiwala, at palalain ang tunggalian sa sahod at presyo.
choices.B: Inaalis nito ang lahat ng utang nang walang epekto
choices.D: Palaging pinapataas ng inflation ang tunay na halaga ng ipon

questions.note: Economic shocks can erode legitimacy and intensify conflict.

questions.question: Bakit hindi sapat ang teknolohikal na kalamangan upang ipaliwanag ang pananakop ng isang imperyo?

choices.A: Dahil hindi nakaaapekto ang teknolohiya sa digmaan
choices.B: Dahil iisang salik lang ang sanhi ng pananakop
choices.C: Dahil laging mas maliit ang imperyo
choices.D: Mahalaga rin ang alyansa, sakit, lokal na tunggalian, logistik, at institusyon.

questions.note: Historical outcomes are multicausal.

questions.question: Ano ang ipinahihiwatig ng paglaganap ng mga nasyonalistikong kilusan matapos ang Ikalawang Digmaang Pandaigdig?

choices.B: Lahat ng kolonya ay naging malaya sa iisang araw
choices.C: Walang epekto ang digmaan sa mga imperyo
choices.D: Humina ang ilang imperyo at lumakas ang mga kahilingan para sa sariling pagpapasya, bagaman magkakaiba ang lokal na dahilan.

questions.note: Decolonization followed different political paths.

questions.question: Paano dapat suriin ang pahayag ng isang pinuno na ang pananakop ay “sibilisasyon”?

choices.A: Ituring itong totoo dahil opisyal ang nagsabi
choices.B: Tanggapin ito bilang neutral na paglalarawan
choices.C: Huwag tingnan ang mga nasakop na tao
choices.D: Ituring itong ideolohikal na katwiran at ihambing sa aktuwal na patakaran at karanasan ng nasakop.

questions.note: Imperial rhetoric should be tested against evidence and affected populations.

questions.question: Bakit maaaring magkaiba ang legal na pag-aalis ng pagkaalipin at ang aktuwal na kalayaan?

choices.A: Dahil walang batas na nakaaapekto sa lipunan
choices.B: Dahil agad na nawawala ang hindi pagkakapantay-pantay
choices.C: Maaaring manatili ang sapilitang paggawa, utang, diskriminasyon, at kawalan ng lupa matapos ang pormal na pagbabago.
choices.D: Dahil ang pagkaalipin ay hindi kailanman legal

questions.note: Formal emancipation does not automatically dismantle coercive structures.

questions.question: Bakit nakatulong ang pagbuo ng mga pambansang estado sa pag-unlad ng ilang industriyal na ekonomiya, ngunit hindi ito sapat na paliwanag?

choices.A: Dahil walang papel ang estado sa ekonomiya
choices.B: Dahil ang industriyalisasyon ay nangyayari lamang sa mga imperyo
choices.C: Maaari nitong pag-isahin ang merkado at batas, ngunit mahalaga rin ang kapital, enerhiya, paggawa, at teknolohiya.
choices.D: Dahil pare-pareho ang industrialization sa lahat ng bansa

questions.note: Institutional integration is one condition among several.

questions.question: Ano ang ipinakikita ng paghahambing ng Haitian Revolution at American Revolution tungkol sa kalayaan?

choices.B: Parehong pinanatili ng dalawa ang iisang sistemang panlipunan
choices.C: Walang kinalaman ang pagkaalipin sa Haiti
choices.D: Maaaring magkaiba ang saklaw ng kalayaan: ang Haitian Revolution ay tuwirang humamon sa pagkaalipin at kolonyal na rasismo.

questions.note: Comparative history highlights different groups included or excluded from liberty.

questions.question: Paano nakaambag ang Treaty of Versailles sa kawalang-katatagan nang hindi ito nag-iisang sanhi ng Ikalawang Digmaang Pandaigdig?

choices.A: Ito ang nagtatag ng United Nations
choices.B: Wala itong anumang epekto sa politika
choices.C: Lumikha ito ng mga hinaing at pagbabago sa hangganan na sinamantala ng mga kilusang ekstremista kasabay ng krisis at ibang salik.
choices.D: Awtomatiko nitong sinimulan ang digmaan sa araw ng pagpirma

questions.note: The treaty interacted with later economic and political crises.

questions.question: Bakit hindi dapat ipakahulugan ang Cold War bilang walang direktang digmaan saanman?

choices.A: Dahil hindi sangkot ang anumang bansa
choices.B: Dahil ang Cold War ay isang kasunduan sa kalakalan
choices.C: Nagkaroon ng proxy wars at marahas na tunggalian sa ibang bansa kahit umiwas ang dalawang superpower sa tuwirang malawakang digmaan sa isa’t isa.

questions.note: The conflict was global and often indirect.

questions.question: Ano ang kahalagahan ng Meiji Restoration sa pag-unlad ng Japan?

choices.A: Tinapos nito ang lahat ng modernisasyon
choices.B: Ibinalik nito ang kapangyarihan sa Tokugawa shogunate
choices.C: Binago nito ang sentral na pamahalaan at pinabilis ang reporma sa militar, edukasyon, at industriya.
choices.D: Ginawang kolonya ng China ang Japan

questions.note: Modernization was state-led and uneven, and later tied to imperial expansion.

questions.question: Bakit dapat iwasang ipaliwanag ang Rebolusyong Pranses bilang simpleng “galit ng mahihirap”?

choices.B: Kasama sa mga sanhi ang krisis sa pananalapi, hindi pantay na pribilehiyo, ideya ng soberanya, at tunggalian ng mga elite.
choices.C: Dahil iisang uri lamang ang lumahok

questions.note: Multiple social and institutional pressures converged.

questions.question: Paano binago ng transatlantic slave trade ang mga ekonomiya sa magkabilang panig ng Atlantiko?

choices.A: Ang epekto ay sa Europa lamang
choices.B: Nagpalaya ito sa lahat ng manggagawa
choices.C: Walang kaugnayan ito sa produksyon ng asukal o bulak
choices.D: Nag-ugnay ito sa produksyon ng plantasyon, pinansiya, kalakalan, at sapilitang paglipat ng milyun-milyong Aprikano.

questions.note: It was a transregional system with profound human and economic effects.

questions.question: Bakit mahalagang pag-ibahin ang pagbagsak ng imperyong Ottoman at ang paglikha ng mga bagong estado pagkatapos ng 1918?

choices.B: Walang kinalaman ang mga kapangyarihang Europeo
choices.C: Hindi simpleng napalitan ng mga estado ang imperyo; ang mga hangganan at pamamahala ay hinubog ng digmaan, mandatong kapangyarihan, at lokal na kilusan.
choices.D: Pare-pareho ang hangganan bago at pagkatapos

questions.note: State formation was contested and shaped by external and local forces.

questions.question: Ano ang pinakamalakas na paliwanag kung bakit kumalat ang mga rebolusyonaryong ideya sa ika-18 at ika-19 na siglo?

choices.A: Dahil pare-pareho ang kultura ng mga bansa
choices.D: Pinabilis ng imprenta, edukasyon, kalakalan, migrasyon, at mga digmaan ang paglipat ng ideya sa pagitan ng lipunan.

questions.note: Ideas moved through networks and were adapted locally.

questions.question: Paano nagkakaiba ang pag-unlad ng suffrage sa iba’t ibang bansa?

choices.A: Awtomatikong nagdala ng suffrage ang industriyalisasyon
choices.B: Pare-parehong petsa ang pagboto ng kababaihan sa lahat ng bansa
choices.D: Nakasalalay ito sa organisasyon ng kilusan, sistemang pampolitika, digmaan, at depinisyon ng pagkamamamayan.

questions.note: Political rights expanded through different struggles and institutions.

questions.question: Why did the Atlantic revolutions produce different outcomes for slavery and citizenship despite shared language about liberty?

choices.B: Ideas of liberty had one fixed meaning everywhere
choices.C: They all abolished slavery in the same year
choices.D: Political coalitions, economic interests, racial hierarchies, and the groups included in citizenship differed.

questions.note: Shared slogans were reinterpreted through local power structures.

questions.question: A state industrializes rapidly but most workers see little improvement in living standards. Which conclusion is best supported?

choices.A: Industrial output alone cannot establish broad welfare gains; wages, working conditions, prices, and distribution must be examined.
choices.B: Every worker must have become poorer

questions.note: Aggregate growth and distributional outcomes are distinct.

questions.question: Why did the Congress of Vienna restore monarchies yet fail to erase revolutionary politics?

choices.A: It prohibited all political debate permanently
choices.B: It rebuilt a diplomatic balance but could not remove the social and ideological changes that had spread.
choices.D: It had no influence on borders

questions.note: Restoration of rulers did not restore the pre-revolutionary world completely.

questions.question: How did the Opium Wars expose a conflict between Qing sovereignty and European commercial demands?

choices.A: The wars ended all foreign trade
choices.B: China voluntarily joined the European Union
choices.C: Military coercion forced treaty arrangements that constrained Chinese control over trade and ports.
choices.D: The conflict concerned only land borders in Europe

questions.note: Unequal treaties altered jurisdiction and commercial access.

questions.question: Why can the fall of the Western Roman Empire not be reduced to “barbarian invasion”?

choices.B: Fiscal pressures, political instability, military changes, and regional transformations interacted with migrations and invasions.
choices.C: The empire had no economic system

questions.note: Multicausal explanations better fit long-term institutional change.

questions.question: What does the contrast between the Soviet collapse and the breakup of Yugoslavia warn historians against?

choices.B: Similar broad pressures can produce different outcomes depending on institutions, nationalism, leadership, and violence.

questions.note: Context mediates broad structural pressures.

questions.question: Why did colonial borders often generate post-independence conflicts?

choices.A: Borders could join rival communities or divide connected ones without matching existing political and social geographies.
choices.B: All borders were drawn by local referenda
choices.C: Every new state inherited identical institutions

questions.note: Colonial boundary-making often disregarded local arrangements.

questions.question: How did the spread of railways change state power as well as commerce?

choices.A: Railways moved goods and people faster and helped governments transport troops, officials, and information.

questions.note: Infrastructure has both economic and administrative effects.

questions.question: Why should the term “Renaissance” not be treated as a sudden, uniform awakening across all of Europe?

choices.B: Its timing, institutions, and cultural effects varied, and it drew on earlier medieval and cross-cultural exchanges.
choices.C: It was unrelated to earlier knowledge
choices.D: It happened everywhere in one decade

questions.note: Period labels simplify gradual and uneven developments.

questions.question: A source praises an empire for building roads but omits forced labor. What is the strongest analysis?

choices.A: The praise proves the empire was benevolent
choices.B: The roads must therefore be fictional
choices.C: Omission proves the author knew nothing
choices.D: The account may describe real infrastructure while excluding the coercive conditions and costs of its construction.

questions.note: A critical reading examines both claims and silences.

questions.question: Why is it misleading to treat the Industrial Revolution as a single invention-driven event?

choices.A: One invention instantly transformed every society
choices.B: Industrialization was identical in every region
choices.C: It depended on interacting changes in energy, finance, labor, institutions, markets, and technology over time.

questions.note: Industrialization was a systemic transition, not a single breakthrough.

questions.question: How can a revolution expand political participation while also narrowing it for some groups?

choices.A: Exclusion ends automatically after a constitution
choices.B: New institutions may broaden representation for some while maintaining exclusions based on race, class, gender, or property.
choices.D: Participation can only rise for everyone equally

questions.note: Political inclusion is often uneven and contested.

questions.question: Why did the post-1945 international order combine decolonization with continued economic dependency in some countries?

choices.C: Political sovereignty did not automatically change trade patterns, capital ownership, debt, or security relationships.

questions.note: Political and economic independence are related but distinct.

questions.question: What does the failure of appeasement in the late 1930s suggest about concessions to expansionist powers?

choices.C: Military force is always the only answer
choices.D: Concessions can fail when they do not change the aggressor’s aims or credible expectations about future resistance.

questions.note: The effect of concessions depends on goals, incentives, and credibility.

questions.question: Why did the Haitian Revolution challenge the universal claims of the French Revolution?

choices.A: Enslaved people demanded that liberty and equality apply beyond the racial and colonial limits tolerated by many revolutionaries.
choices.B: The revolution opposed every idea of equality
choices.C: France had abolished all slavery before 1789
choices.D: Haiti was not influenced by revolutionary ideas

questions.note: It exposed contradictions between universal rights and colonial practice.

questions.question: How can a state’s census become a tool of power rather than a neutral count?

choices.A: A census always records natural categories
choices.B: Categories can define identities, allocate resources, and make some groups visible while marginalizing others.

questions.note: Classification is part of governance.

questions.question: Why did the Mongol Empire facilitate exchange without creating a culturally uniform Eurasia?

choices.A: The empire banned all cultural exchange
choices.D: Conquest and protected routes increased movement, but local languages, religions, and institutions persisted.

questions.note: Connectivity does not require uniformity.

questions.question: What makes a “proxy war” analytically different from a direct war between superpowers?

choices.D: Outside powers support local combatants, while local aims and conditions still shape the conflict.

questions.note: The label should not erase local causes or actors.

questions.question: Why might the same economic crisis strengthen authoritarian movements in one country but not another?

choices.A: Economic crises always have identical effects
choices.C: Political institutions, organized opposition, elite choices, and public trust mediate how crises are translated into politics.

questions.note: Similar shocks can produce divergent outcomes.

questions.question: How should historians assess whether a treaty “caused” a later war?

choices.A: Treat any later war as inevitable
choices.D: Trace mechanisms linking treaty terms to later decisions and compare them with other contributing causes.

questions.note: Temporal sequence is not sufficient causal evidence.

questions.question: A historian argues that empire-building was driven only by economic profit. What evidence would most directly challenge this monocausal claim?

choices.A: Evidence that profit existed in one colony
choices.B: Evidence that strategic, ideological, domestic political, and security motives independently shaped decisions alongside profit.
choices.C: A map showing the empire was large
choices.D: A speech that uses the word “trade” once

questions.note: A monocausal thesis must account for independent motives and variation.

questions.question: Why is the “rise of the West” framework criticized when it treats European development as internally generated and inevitable?

choices.B: It can obscure global exchanges, colonial extraction, contingent choices, and parallel developments elsewhere.

questions.note: The framework risks turning a contingent outcome into a predetermined one.

questions.question: How can historians distinguish a structural cause from a trigger in a revolution?

choices.A: A trigger must occur decades earlier
choices.C: A structural cause creates long-term vulnerability; a trigger precipitates action under those conditions.

questions.note: Both levels are needed to explain timing and underlying instability.

questions.question: Why does comparing legal texts with enforcement records matter when studying abolition?

choices.A: Enforcement records cannot be historical evidence
choices.C: Abolition has no relation to labor
choices.D: It reveals whether formal prohibition changed practice or whether coercion persisted through other legal and economic forms.

questions.note: Law on paper and lived conditions can diverge.

questions.question: A nationalist movement claims to represent “the people,” but records show internal class and regional disputes. What is the best conclusion?

choices.C: National unity was a political claim negotiated among groups with different interests, not a fixed fact.

questions.note: Nationalism can unite and conceal differences at once.

questions.question: Why should the end of an empire be studied through continuities as well as formal dates of independence?

choices.A: Administrative practices, elite networks, economic dependencies, and borders may persist after legal sovereignty changes.
choices.D: Empires end only when all customs vanish

questions.note: Political rupture and structural continuity can coexist.

questions.question: What is the strongest way to test a claim that a technological invention “caused” social transformation?

choices.B: Assume every society adopted it equally
choices.D: Show the mechanism of adoption and impact, compare contexts with different adoption rates, and consider complementary conditions.

questions.note: Causal claims require mechanisms and comparative evidence.

questions.question: Why can an empire’s administrative records simultaneously be useful and deeply biased?

choices.B: They preserve detailed information but were created for governance, taxation, surveillance, or control.
choices.C: Bias makes every recorded fact unusable

questions.note: Purpose shapes records without automatically invalidating them.

questions.question: How does a global-history approach alter the explanation of a local revolution?

choices.B: It traces cross-border flows of ideas, commodities, people, and military pressure without erasing local agency.
choices.D: It assumes every local event was controlled abroad

questions.note: Global connections and local choices interact.

questions.question: What is the strongest test of a claim that a historical policy succeeded?

choices.D: Define the intended outcome, measure results across affected groups, and compare with plausible alternatives or counterfactuals.

questions.note: Success requires explicit criteria and evidence of effects.

questions.question: Why are many major cities located near coasts or navigable rivers?

choices.B: They historically reduce transport costs and connect settlements to trade networks
choices.C: Coasts always have the mildest climate

questions.note: Water transport historically moved bulky goods relatively efficiently.

questions.question: Which map projection property is most important when comparing the true relative sizes of countries?

choices.C: Showing all routes as straight lines

questions.note: Equal-area projections preserve relative area, though they distort other properties.

questions.question: Why is it usually cooler at a mountain summit than at its base?

choices.A: Gravity removes all heat from high places
choices.B: Air pressure decreases with altitude, and rising air expands and cools
choices.C: The Sun is farther away by a meaningful amount

questions.note: Lower pressure allows air to expand; the environmental lapse rate generally lowers temperature with altitude.

questions.question: Which country has the most people in South America?
questions.note: Brazil has over 200 million people.

questions.question: Mount Everest is part of which mountain range?
questions.note: K2 is in the Karakoram.

questions.question: Which desert covers much of northern Africa?
questions.note: The Kalahari is in southern Africa; the Gobi is in Asia.

questions.question: Which country is shaped like a boot?
questions.note: The Italian peninsula's shape resembles a boot.

questions.question: What is the capital of Australia?
questions.note: Canberra was purpose-built as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.

questions.question: Which is the largest country by area?
questions.note: About 17.1 million km²; Canada is second.

questions.question: Which line divides Earth into Northern and Southern Hemispheres?
questions.note: The Prime Meridian divides East and West.

questions.question: A coastal desert lies beside a cold ocean current. How can the current contribute to aridity?

choices.B: It cools lower air, stabilizing the atmosphere and limiting rising moist air
choices.C: It increases evaporation enough to guarantee rain

questions.note: Cold currents can stabilize air and suppress convection, while other factors also shape rainfall.

questions.question: Why can a country's population density be high near a river delta?

choices.A: Deltas are always above flood risk
choices.B: Flat land, fertile sediments, and transport access can support dense settlement despite flood hazards

questions.note: Deltas offer agricultural and transport advantages but also serious environmental risks.

questions.question: What happens to local solar time as longitude increases eastward?

choices.A: It becomes earlier by four minutes per degree
choices.B: It becomes later by roughly four minutes per degree
choices.D: It changes only at the Equator

questions.note: Earth rotates 360° in about 24 hours, or approximately 4 minutes per degree.

questions.question: The Strait of Gibraltar connects the Atlantic Ocean with the…
questions.note: It separates Spain from Morocco.

questions.question: What is the smallest country in the world by area?
questions.note: About 0.44 km²; Monaco is second.

questions.question: Which country does NOT border Germany?
questions.note: Austria and Switzerland separate Germany from Italy.

questions.question: Mount Kilimanjaro is in which country?
questions.note: It sits near the Kenyan border but inside Tanzania.

questions.question: What is the capital of Canada?
questions.note: Toronto is Canada's largest city.

questions.question: Which body of water lies between Saudi Arabia and northeast Africa?
questions.note: The Persian Gulf is on Saudi Arabia's east side.

questions.question: Which U.S. state is the largest by area?
questions.note: Alaska is more than twice the size of Texas.

questions.question: Why can two places at the same latitude have very different climates?

choices.B: Elevation, ocean currents, prevailing winds, continentality, and relief modify climate
choices.D: Local geography affects rainfall but never temperature

questions.note: Latitude is important but does not determine climate by itself.

questions.question: A mountain range runs perpendicular to moist prevailing winds. Which pattern is most likely?

choices.A: Equal rainfall on both sides in every season
choices.B: More precipitation on the windward slope and drier conditions in the lee
choices.C: More precipitation only in the rain shadow

questions.note: Orographic lifting promotes windward precipitation; descending air on the leeward side is often drier.

questions.question: Why might a country with a large total area still have relatively little arable land?

choices.A: Area and land quality are unrelated in every case
choices.B: Much of its territory may be desert, mountain, permafrost, or otherwise unsuitable for cultivation
choices.D: Arable land depends only on population

questions.note: Total land area does not equal land suitable for crops.

questions.question: The Danube River empties into which sea?
questions.note: Its delta is on the Romania–Ukraine coast.

questions.question: Which city lies on two continents?
questions.note: The Bosporus splits it between Europe and Asia.

questions.question: What is the capital of Brazil?
questions.note: Brasília replaced Rio de Janeiro as capital in 1960.

questions.question: Which is the deepest lake in the world?
questions.note: Over 1,600 m deep, in Siberia.

questions.question: Which north–south range forms much of the conventional Europe–Asia boundary?
questions.note: The Caucasus run east–west further south.

questions.question: What is the largest island that is not a continent?
questions.note: About 2.17 million km²; New Guinea is second.

questions.question: Which river forms much of the U.S.–Mexico border?
questions.note: Called the Río Bravo in Mexico.

questions.question: A city grows rapidly on a delta with subsiding land and rising sea level. Which combined risk is most important?

choices.A: Relative sea-level rise increases flood exposure, especially where drainage and protective infrastructure are inadequate.
choices.C: Sea-level rise affects only rocky coasts

questions.note: Risk reflects physical processes plus exposure and infrastructure.

questions.question: Why can two places at the same latitude have very different climates?

choices.A: Elevation, ocean currents, prevailing winds, continentality, and relief alter temperature and precipitation.
choices.B: Latitude alone fixes every climate variable
choices.D: Local geography has no climatic effect

questions.note: Latitude is important but not sufficient.

questions.question: A rain shadow produces a wet windward slope and dry leeward region. What mechanism explains it?

choices.A: The leeward side receives more condensation
choices.C: Air warms as it rises and gains moisture
choices.D: Moist air rises and cools on the windward side, then descends and warms after losing moisture.

questions.note: Orographic lifting and descending air create the contrast.

questions.question: Why does a choropleth map using raw population totals risk misleading comparisons?

choices.B: Population totals are unrelated to geography
choices.C: Large areas or differently sized populations can dominate; rates or normalized values may better answer the question.

questions.note: Map design must match the comparison being made.

questions.question: A country’s fertility rate falls while its total population continues growing. What explains this?

choices.B: Population momentum: large younger cohorts continue entering reproductive ages, while life expectancy may also rise.
choices.C: Migration is the only possible explanation

questions.note: Demographic age structure can delay population decline.

questions.question: Why might a river basin be a better unit for water management than political boundaries?

choices.C: Water flows across jurisdictions, so upstream decisions affect downstream supply, flooding, and pollution.

questions.note: Hydrological systems rarely align neatly with political borders.

questions.question: How can a country be resource-rich yet remain economically vulnerable?

choices.A: Dependence on a few volatile exports can expose public revenue and jobs to price shocks and governance problems.

questions.note: Resource abundance does not ensure resilient institutions or diversification.

questions.question: Why do urban heat islands often intensify at night?

choices.D: Built surfaces store heat and release it, while reduced vegetation and altered airflow limit cooling.

questions.note: Urban form changes heat storage and cooling.

questions.question: A map shows high disease rates near a road network. Why is this not proof that roads caused the disease?

choices.A: The pattern may reflect access to clinics, population density, reporting, or other confounders; causal evidence is needed.

questions.note: Spatial association alone does not establish causality.

questions.question: Why can a country’s GDP rise while regional inequality worsens?

choices.A: GDP includes only the poorest region
choices.B: Growth may concentrate in particular sectors and cities rather than being distributed evenly.

questions.note: Aggregate output hides distribution.

questions.question: A coastal city faces stronger storms, more paved surfaces, and declining wetlands. Why does flood risk compound?

choices.A: Storm surge and rainfall increase water input while impervious cover speeds runoff and wetland loss removes natural storage.

questions.note: Hazards interact with land-use change and loss of buffers.

questions.question: Why can the same rainfall total cause a flash flood in one watershed but little flooding in another?

choices.C: Slope, soil saturation, vegetation, drainage, basin shape, and rainfall intensity control runoff timing.
choices.D: Rainfall totals alone determine flood peaks

questions.note: Hydrology depends on more than total precipitation.

questions.question: How can a population pyramid reveal future pressure on public services?

choices.B: A large child cohort implies future school demand and, later, labor-market entry; an aging profile implies greater care needs.
choices.C: Age structure has no policy relevance

questions.note: Age cohorts move through services over time.

questions.question: Why might a new highway increase deforestation even if the road itself occupies little land?

choices.A: Deforestation only occurs at road edges
choices.C: It can improve access, raise land values, and enable settlement, logging, and agriculture along the corridor.

questions.note: Infrastructure can induce land-use change beyond its footprint.

questions.question: A map projection preserves angles but greatly enlarges high latitudes. Which use is it least suited for?

choices.C: Comparing the relative land areas of countries.

questions.note: Conformal projections distort area, especially at high latitudes.

questions.question: Why can glacier retreat threaten dry regions far from the glacier?

choices.C: Seasonal meltwater may sustain rivers during dry periods, so reduced ice storage changes downstream supply.

questions.note: Mountain water sources can support distant downstream users.

questions.question: What is the main geographic limitation of treating a country’s average rainfall as a measure of water security?

choices.C: Rainfall varies seasonally and spatially, while storage, infrastructure, demand, and water quality determine usable supply.

questions.note: Water security is a systems problem, not a single climate statistic.

questions.question: Why may a megacity’s informal settlements grow on hazard-prone land?

choices.A: All hazard land is legally free
choices.B: Affordable central land is scarce, and residents may trade lower cost or proximity to work against greater risk.
choices.D: Urban land markets do not matter

questions.note: Risk exposure reflects housing access and unequal urban development.

questions.question: How can trade winds and ocean currents jointly shape a region’s rainfall?

choices.B: Rainfall is independent of ocean temperature
choices.C: Winds transport moisture while currents alter the temperature and stability of the air above the ocean.
choices.D: Currents act only below the seabed

questions.note: Atmosphere and ocean exchange heat and moisture.

questions.question: Why should migration statistics distinguish net migration from total flows?

choices.A: Large numbers can enter and leave simultaneously, leaving a small net change but substantial movement.
choices.B: Departures are not part of migration
choices.C: Total flows always equal net change
choices.D: Net migration counts every arrival twice

questions.note: Net balance and gross movement answer different questions.

questions.question: A region’s agricultural output rises after irrigation expansion, but groundwater levels fall. What is the strongest systems-level conclusion?

choices.A: Higher output proves the system is sustainable
choices.C: Short-term gains may be unsustainable if extraction exceeds recharge, requiring analysis of demand, recharge, and crop choices.
choices.D: Groundwater levels do not affect agriculture

questions.note: Resource use must be assessed against renewal rates.

questions.question: Why is a border river especially vulnerable to political conflict during drought?

choices.A: Rivers are always governed by one country
choices.D: Upstream control, competing demands, weak agreements, and unequal bargaining power can turn reduced flow into a distribution dispute.

questions.note: Scarcity interacts with institutions and power.

questions.question: How can a city reduce heat exposure without merely shifting it to poorer neighborhoods?

choices.B: Combine citywide shade and cooling with equitable siting, tenant protections, and monitoring of displacement and energy costs.
choices.D: Plant trees only in high-income districts

questions.note: Climate adaptation must consider distributional effects.

questions.question: Why can a country’s food imports rise even while domestic production grows?

choices.A: Demand may grow faster, diets may shift, or domestic production may specialize in crops not matching consumption.
choices.C: Trade cannot coexist with local farming
choices.D: Population has no effect on demand

questions.note: Production volume and food-system balance differ.

questions.question: A landslide map predicts danger using slope alone. What major weakness does it have?

choices.B: It omits triggers and susceptibility factors such as rainfall, geology, vegetation, and human modification.
choices.C: Landslides occur only on flat land

questions.note: Hazard assessment needs multiple interacting variables.

questions.question: Why can national averages hide a climate-vulnerability hotspot?

choices.A: Vulnerability is identical across a country
choices.D: Exposure, adaptive capacity, infrastructure, and hazards vary sharply between regions and social groups.

questions.note: Risk is spatially uneven.

questions.question: What is the difference between a hazard and a disaster in geographic analysis?

choices.A: Every hazard automatically becomes a disaster
choices.B: A hazard is a potentially damaging event; disaster outcomes depend on exposure, vulnerability, and response capacity.
choices.C: A disaster is only a weather event

questions.note: Disaster severity is socially and spatially mediated.

questions.question: Why can desalination solve a supply problem but create another environmental or economic problem?

choices.C: It creates freshwater without energy or waste
choices.D: It requires energy and produces concentrated brine, while high costs may limit access.

questions.note: Technological supply must be evaluated across its full system.

questions.question: How can a country have high water availability but poor household access?

choices.B: Water may be polluted, distant, seasonally unavailable, or inaccessible because of infrastructure and affordability.
choices.C: Pipes do not affect water access

questions.note: Physical abundance and effective access differ.

questions.question: Why does a map of election results by district risk the ecological fallacy?

choices.A: District-level patterns do not establish how each individual voted or why.
choices.D: Every voter in a district votes alike

questions.note: Group-level relationships cannot automatically be assigned to individuals.

questions.question: A student doubles the mass of a cart while keeping its net force constant. According to Newton's second law, what happens to its acceleration?
questions.note: Since a = F/m, doubling mass at constant net force halves acceleration.

questions.question: Why does a metal spoon feel colder than a wooden spoon in the same room?

choices.A: The metal must have a lower temperature
choices.B: Metal conducts heat away from the hand faster than wood

questions.note: Thermal conductivity changes the rate of heat transfer, not necessarily the object's temperature.

questions.question: A solution changes blue litmus paper to red. What can be concluded most directly?
questions.note: Blue litmus turning red indicates acidic conditions.

questions.question: Which part of an animal cell holds most of its DNA?
questions.note: Ribosomes build proteins; the membrane encloses the cell.

questions.question: Which force keeps the planets in orbit around the Sun?
questions.note: Inertia alone would send planets off in straight lines.

questions.question: At sea level, water boils at what temperature?
questions.note: Equal to 212 °F.

questions.question: Which is the largest planet in our solar system?
questions.note: Jupiter is over 300 times Earth's mass.

questions.question: What is the hardest natural substance?
questions.note: Diamond is 10 on the Mohs scale.

questions.question: How many bones are in the adult human body?
questions.note: Babies have about 270–300 that fuse over time.

questions.question: What kind of animal is a whale?
questions.note: Whales breathe air and nurse their young.

questions.question: A plant is kept in darkness for several days but is watered normally. Which process is directly limited first?
questions.note: Light is required for photosynthesis, although respiration continues.

questions.question: Why does a sealed syringe become harder to compress as its plunger is pushed inward?

choices.B: The same gas occupies less volume, increasing pressure through more frequent particle-wall collisions
choices.C: The gas loses all kinetic energy
choices.D: The number of gas particles increases automatically

questions.note: Compression reduces volume and raises pressure for a fixed amount of gas at roughly constant temperature.

questions.question: A 12 V battery is connected across a 6 Ω resistor. What current flows through the resistor?
questions.note: Ohm's law gives I = V/R = 12/6 = 2 A.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for sodium?
questions.note: From Latin 'natrium'. S is sulfur.

questions.question: Through which material does sound travel fastest?
questions.note: Sound is fastest in solids and cannot travel through a vacuum.

questions.question: Which blood cells fight infection?
questions.note: Red cells carry oxygen; platelets help clotting.

questions.question: Which planet has the hottest surface?
questions.note: Venus's thick CO₂ atmosphere traps heat (~465 °C), hotter than Mercury.

questions.question: Which subatomic particle has a negative charge?
questions.note: Protons and positrons are positive; neutrons are neutral.

questions.question: Which type of rock forms when magma cools?
questions.note: Clastic rocks are a kind of sedimentary rock.

questions.question: What is the pH of pure water at 25 °C?
questions.note: Neutral is pH 7.

questions.question: A ball is thrown straight upward. At its highest point, ignoring air resistance, which statement is correct?

choices.A: Velocity and acceleration are both zero
choices.B: Velocity is zero but acceleration is downward
choices.C: Velocity is upward and acceleration is zero
choices.D: Velocity and acceleration are both upward

questions.note: The instantaneous velocity is zero at the top, but gravity still accelerates the ball downward.

questions.question: A mutation changes one DNA base but does not change the amino acid sequence. Which explanation is most likely?

choices.A: The genetic code is degenerate, so multiple codons can specify the same amino acid

questions.note: A synonymous mutation can change a codon without changing the encoded amino acid.

questions.question: Why does adding a catalyst increase reaction rate without changing the reaction's equilibrium constant?

choices.A: It raises the energy of all products
choices.B: It lowers activation barriers for forward and reverse reactions but does not change the equilibrium energy difference
choices.C: It changes the chemical formula of the reactants

questions.note: A catalyst changes kinetics, not the thermodynamic equilibrium constant at a given temperature.

questions.question: Which element has atomic number 6?
questions.note: Boron is 5, nitrogen 7, oxygen 8.

questions.question: In which atmospheric layer is the ozone layer found?
questions.note: Roughly 15–35 km up.

questions.question: What type of energy does a stretched rubber band store?
questions.note: Released as kinetic energy when let go.

questions.question: What is the shape of a DNA molecule?
questions.note: Described by Watson and Crick in 1953.

questions.question: Which planet has the shortest day?
questions.note: Jupiter rotates in about 10 hours; Saturn in about 10.7.

questions.question: Which vitamin does your skin make in sunlight?
questions.note: UVB light triggers vitamin D production.

questions.question: Which of these is a noble gas?
questions.note: Noble gases (group 18) are very unreactive.

questions.question: A study finds plants grow taller under blue light but have less total biomass. Which interpretation is strongest?

choices.A: Height alone is not a complete measure of growth; biomass and other outcomes suggest a different response.

questions.note: Operational definitions determine what “growth” means.

questions.question: A reaction speeds up when temperature rises. What explanation best fits collision theory?

choices.A: Temperature changes the atoms into a new element
choices.C: Particles have greater average kinetic energy, increasing the fraction of collisions that exceed activation energy.

questions.note: Higher temperature increases effective collision frequency.

questions.question: A ball moves at constant speed around a circle. Why is it accelerating?

choices.B: Its velocity direction continuously changes, even though speed stays constant.

questions.note: Velocity includes direction, so changing direction is acceleration.

questions.question: Why is a control group important in an experiment testing a fertilizer?

choices.A: It guarantees the hypothesis is true
choices.B: It provides a comparison for estimating changes not attributable to the fertilizer.
choices.C: It removes the need for replication

questions.note: Controls help isolate the treatment effect.

questions.question: A food web loses a top predator and herbivore numbers rise. What is a plausible indirect consequence?

choices.C: Greater herbivory may reduce plant populations and alter other species interactions.
choices.D: Plants must increase in every case

questions.note: Trophic cascades can transmit effects across levels.

questions.question: Why does increasing sample size usually improve an estimate but not automatically remove bias?

choices.A: More observations reduce random error, while systematic selection or measurement errors can persist.
choices.C: Random error and bias are identical
choices.D: Bias disappears when n exceeds ten

questions.note: Precision and validity are distinct.

questions.question: A metal wire is heated while its ends are free. Why does it usually lengthen?

choices.A: The wire loses all internal energy
choices.D: Greater thermal motion increases average spacing in the material.

questions.note: Thermal expansion reflects changes in average interatomic spacing.

questions.question: Why can antibiotics fail against a viral infection?

choices.D: Antibiotics target bacterial structures or processes that viruses do not possess in the same way.

questions.note: Treatment must target the biology of the pathogen.

questions.question: A fossil layer lies below another in undisturbed rock. What is the strongest basic inference?

choices.B: The lower layer must contain simpler organisms
choices.C: The upper layer is always volcanic
choices.D: The lower layer is generally older, unless the sequence has been disturbed.

questions.note: Relative dating relies on superposition and geological context.

questions.question: Why does a population with limited genetic variation face elevated risk from a new pathogen?

choices.B: Fewer individuals may carry variants that provide resistance, reducing the population’s adaptive options.

questions.note: Genetic diversity can influence population-level resilience.

questions.question: A drug reduces symptoms in a trial but the treatment group was younger on average. What is the main concern?

choices.A: The trial proves the drug works
choices.B: Age is a potential confounder that may explain some of the observed difference.

questions.note: Groups should be comparable or adjusted for confounders.

questions.question: A planet’s orbital speed increases near its star. Which principle best explains this?

choices.A: The planet gains mass from sunlight
choices.B: It moves faster near periapsis as gravitational potential energy converts to kinetic energy while angular momentum is conserved.
choices.C: Orbital speed is constant in every elliptical orbit

questions.note: Elliptical orbits have varying speed.

questions.question: A population grows rapidly, then growth slows as resources become limited. Which model may describe this pattern?

choices.D: Logistic growth, where growth rate decreases as population approaches carrying capacity.

questions.note: Density-dependent limits slow population growth.

questions.question: Why can two medicines with equal average effectiveness have different clinical value?

choices.C: They may differ in side effects, duration, interactions, patient subgroups, and uncertainty of evidence.
choices.D: Side effects do not affect treatment

questions.note: Clinical decisions consider benefits, harms, and context.

questions.question: A solution’s pH changes from 3 to 5. By what factor does hydrogen-ion concentration change?

choices.A: It increases by a factor of 100
choices.B: It decreases by a factor of 2
choices.C: It decreases by a factor of 100.
choices.D: It decreases by a factor of 10

questions.note: Each pH unit represents a tenfold change; two units means 100-fold.

questions.question: Why might a species survive a short heatwave but decline under repeated heatwaves?

choices.A: Survival of one event guarantees long-term stability
choices.C: Population size is unrelated to recovery
choices.D: Repeated stress may reduce reproduction and recovery time, producing cumulative population effects.

questions.note: Acute survival differs from long-term demographic resilience.

questions.question: A satellite remains in orbit rather than falling straight down. What best explains this?

choices.A: The satellite is beyond Earth’s gravity
choices.B: There is no inertia in space
choices.C: Gravity continuously bends its path while its tangential velocity carries it forward.
choices.D: Gravity does not act in orbit

questions.note: Orbit is continuous free fall with sufficient sideways velocity.

questions.question: Why does a catalyst speed a reaction without changing the equilibrium constant?

choices.C: It adds energy permanently to products
choices.D: It lowers activation barriers for forward and reverse pathways but does not change the reaction’s thermodynamic energy difference.

questions.note: Catalysts alter kinetics, not equilibrium thermodynamics.

questions.question: A test has high sensitivity but low specificity. What is the likely tradeoff?

choices.A: It proves every positive result is true
choices.B: It catches many true cases but may also produce more false positives.
choices.C: It misses nearly all true cases

questions.note: Sensitivity and specificity measure different error types.

questions.question: Why is correlation between screen time and poor sleep insufficient to prove screen time is the sole cause?

choices.A: Stress, schedule, health, and reverse causation may also contribute; causal designs are needed.
choices.B: A large correlation removes all confounders

questions.note: Association requires causal reasoning and alternatives.

questions.question: A researcher tests ten hypotheses and reports only the one with p < .05. What is the key statistical risk?

choices.B: Ten tests guarantee no false positives
choices.C: Multiple testing increases the chance of a false positive when selective reporting is not accounted for.

questions.note: Selective reporting inflates apparent evidence.

questions.question: Why can a species’ fundamental niche be broader than its realized niche?

choices.C: The realized niche always includes every possible habitat
choices.D: Competition, predation, and other biotic interactions may restrict where it persists in nature.

questions.note: Potential tolerances differ from actual ecological distribution.

questions.question: A climate model reproduces past temperatures but performs poorly on a new period. What should researchers examine?

choices.C: The new data must be wrong
choices.D: Overfitting, missing processes, data quality, and whether the model generalizes beyond calibration conditions.

questions.note: Validation tests performance beyond the fitted dataset.

questions.question: Why does a mutation’s effect depend on genetic and environmental context?

choices.A: Every mutation has one universal effect
choices.D: Its impact can interact with other genes, regulation, development, and environmental conditions.

questions.note: Genotype-to-phenotype relationships are context-dependent.

questions.question: A battery’s voltage stays constant while current falls as a load’s resistance rises. Which relation explains it?

choices.A: Voltage equals resistance divided by current
choices.B: Ohm’s law: at constant voltage, current is inversely proportional to resistance.

questions.note: For an ohmic load, I = V/R.

questions.question: Why can an observed increase in biodiversity after restoration be misleading if only total species count is reported?

choices.A: Counts may hide the loss of specialist species, dominance by invasives, or changes in abundance and function.
choices.D: Species count always captures ecosystem health

questions.note: Metrics must match the ecological objective.

questions.question: How does natural selection differ from an individual adapting physiologically during its lifetime?

choices.A: Acclimation changes every population gene frequency
choices.B: Selection occurs only within one lifetime
choices.C: Both always change DNA sequence directly
choices.D: Selection changes trait frequencies across generations; acclimation changes an individual’s response within its lifetime.

questions.note: Evolutionary and physiological timescales differ.

questions.question: Why does energy conservation not mean that every energy transformation is equally useful?

choices.B: Energy can disperse as heat, reducing the fraction available to perform organized work.

questions.note: Energy is conserved while usable energy quality can decrease.

questions.question: A medical study reports a relative risk reduction of 50%, from 2% to 1% absolute risk. Why should both measures be reported?

choices.B: The relative reduction sounds large, while the absolute reduction clarifies the baseline change in probability.
choices.C: The measures cannot both be correct

questions.note: Relative and absolute effects answer different questions.

questions.question: Why does a causal claim from an observational study require more caution than a well-controlled randomized trial?

choices.B: Causation can be read directly from any graph
choices.C: Treatment assignment may be related to confounders in observational data, complicating causal attribution.

questions.note: Design affects how confidently alternatives can be ruled out.

choices.D: Our changing view of its lit half

questions.note: Earth's shadow on the Moon is a lunar eclipse, not a phase.

questions.note: Gravity accelerates all objects equally.

questions.note: Water expands when it freezes.

questions.note: Lower air pressure lets water boil at a lower temperature.

questions.question: Apply scientific reasoning: Why is the daytime sky blue?
questions.note: Rayleigh scattering affects shorter wavelengths most.

questions.note: A series circuit has only one path; a break stops all current.

questions.question: Apply scientific reasoning: Which of these is a chemical change?
questions.note: Rust is a new substance (iron oxide). The others are physical changes.

questions.question: Apply scientific reasoning: What mainly causes Earth's seasons?
questions.note: Earth is actually closest to the Sun in January.

questions.question: Apply scientific reasoning: A ball thrown straight up reaches its highest point. Its acceleration there is…?
questions.note: Velocity is zero at the top, but gravity still accelerates it.

questions.question: Apply scientific reasoning: Which blood type is the universal donor for red blood cells?
questions.note: AB positive is the universal recipient.

questions.question: Apply scientific reasoning: At the same room temperature, why does a metal spoon feel colder than a wooden one?
questions.note: Both are the same temperature; metal draws heat from your hand faster.

questions.question: Apply scientific reasoning: What happens to an animal cell placed in very salty water?
questions.note: Osmosis moves water out toward the saltier side.

questions.question: Apply scientific reasoning: Which planet is less dense than water?
questions.note: Saturn's average density is about 0.69 g/cm³.

choices.A: They are in continuous free fall
choices.D: There is no gravity in orbit

questions.question: Apply scientific reasoning: As a siren moves away from you, its pitch sounds…?
questions.note: The Doppler effect stretches the sound waves.

questions.question: Apply scientific reasoning: Why don't antibiotics cure the common cold?
questions.note: Antibiotics target bacteria, not viruses.

questions.note: Buoyant force = 10 N = weight of equal-volume water, so 30 ÷ 10 = 3.

questions.note: Frequency stays constant, so wavelength shrinks with speed.

questions.question: Apply scientific reasoning: An object moves in a circle at constant speed. Why is it accelerating?
questions.note: Acceleration is any change in velocity, including direction.

questions.note: Fossils like Mesosaurus appear in both South America and Africa.

questions.question: Apply scientific reasoning: Which has more total thermal energy?
questions.note: Temperature is average energy per particle; the tub has far more water.

questions.question: Apply scientific reasoning: If Earth had no Moon, ocean tides would…?
questions.note: The Sun would still cause tides, about half as strong.

questions.note: KE = ½mv², so doubling v quadruples KE.
